messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I run a small independent press. One of our essay collections has sold steadily but not enough to justify a full audiobook. The author proposed releasing six essays as a weekly narrated series, with a print-and-audio bundle at the end. I like the experiment, but our editor, production manager, and board are worried that an open-ended audio project will consume the autumn list.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Frame it as one bounded season with its own authority, cost, release, and evidence rules. Separate editorial approval from recording production, accessibility, distribution, audience measurement, and any later format decision. The pilot should state what the press is committing to now and who decides what follows after the evidence window.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The author will approve every script and can reject an edit that changes meaning. Our senior editor will prepare the scripts and sign the final text. A local actor is available for four recording days in August, enough for all six essays if we keep each episode under twenty-two minutes. The actor has not promised any dates after September.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Write the author veto, editor sign-off, narrator dates, episode limit, and season size into the charter. Keep the text version paired with each recording so listeners and reviewers can see which script was approved. Later narrator availability need not be decided for a six-episode commitment, but the season needs a production response if an August session is lost.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: We can spend $8,400 including narration, studio, mixing, transcript cleanup, cover art, and distribution. The production manager estimates $1,250 per finished episode before marketing. The board will permit up to $9,000 but wants a stop if the first three episodes project above that cap. Marketing has only twelve staff hours a week in September.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Use the $9,000 as a season ceiling and require a forecast after episode three. Assign the production manager to calculate committed and projected cost, and require the publisher to approve any reallocation before work continues. Cap marketing hours in the same tracker so production does not succeed by quietly displacing another book campaign.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Accessibility is non-negotiable. The web producer can publish a corrected transcript with each episode, but needs the locked script four business days before release and the mixed audio two days before. If either arrives late, she wants authority to delay the episode. The author accepts delay but does not want an automated transcript posted as a placeholder.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Make transcript completion a release condition. The web producer should verify the final transcript against the mixed audio and hold publication if the approved text, audio, and transcript do not align. Record the version hashes and sign-offs in the episode checklist. A weekly date can move; the accessibility requirement does not.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: For audience evidence, the distributor can give us completed plays, drop-off by minute, referrals to the book page, bundle purchases, and newsletter signups. It also offers listener-level advertising profiles, which I do not want. The author cares about completion and thoughtful responses, while the board cares about conversion and whether the series reaches readers outside our existing list.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Limit collection to aggregate episode completion, drop-off bands, referral source, bundle purchases, and voluntary newsletter signup. Reject listener-level advertising profiles in the distributor settings. Add a small qualitative channel, such as one optional question on the episode page, and decide in advance which measures inform production adjustments and which wait for the board review.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The sales director worries that releasing six essays will cannibalize the hardcover. The author thinks samples will attract new readers. We cannot settle that in advance. The board asked for checkpoints after episodes two and four, but it does not want a weak first week to cancel a season we have already recorded.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Define the checkpoints by purpose. After episode two, review release operations, transcript timing, listener drop-off, and production forecast; adjust promotion or episode packaging but do not cancel solely on early sales. After episode four, review the same measures plus bundle referrals and remaining cost. Reserve the season-level format decision for a dated board meeting after the evidence window.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The board meeting is October 22, three weeks after the final episode. It will choose among stopping, repeating another bounded season, licensing a full audiobook, or returning to print-only promotion. There will be no automatic continuation. The author and editor can submit their interpretation of the evidence, but the board retains the business-format decision.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Put those four choices, the evidence window, submission date, and board authority into the calendar now. The current charter should end after the six releases and closeout work. That allows the board to select a later format without making the pilot team guess whether silence means continuation.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The actor has warned us that a touring offer could take one August date. The studio can hold a backup day, but only at extra cost. The author is willing to record a short introduction but not whole essays. The editor says that if we bank four episodes before launch, a lost date would be manageable.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Set a minimum bank before the first release and name the response to a shortfall. The production manager can use the backup studio day within the season cap; if fewer than two unreleased episodes remain ready, the publisher can insert a one-week gap and use an approved text excerpt rather than substitute an unapproved narrator. Record who may choose each response.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: We also need version control. The author sometimes improves a sentence after hearing it aloud. The editor can accept punctuation or a correction, but any substantive change must return to the author and then to transcript production. The web producer wants a cutoff because a late revised script can invalidate both the transcript and the mix.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Use one locked-script identifier per episode. Substantive changes after lock require author and editor approval, a new identifier, and a refreshed transcript and mix check. The web producer can delay release when the approved identifier does not match the delivered files. Keep the earlier version in the production record rather than overwriting it.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Here is the operating table: at least four finished episodes before launch; pause scheduling if the ready bank falls below two; transcript and mixed audio due two business days before publication; no episode above twenty-two minutes without editor approval; forecast at episode three must remain within $9,000; no listener profiles; and any substantive text change resets the accessibility checks.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Assign each line to a role and evidence source. Production owns the bank and cost forecast, editorial owns length and text approval, the web producer owns transcript release, the publisher owns pauses and budget changes, and the distributor settings document the privacy limit. Put the checkpoint dates beside those controls.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The distributor just told us one podcast platform may take five days to update an episode. Our own site and the two main platforms update within hours. Marketing wants to promise one universal Friday release. The production manager would rather publish on our site Friday and let the slower platform follow when its feed refreshes.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Define the official release on channels the press controls and disclose that secondary feeds may lag. The web producer can verify the primary channels Friday morning and record the slower platform's eventual appearance. A distribution delay should not trigger a new mix or transcript cycle unless the delivered file itself is wrong.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The production calendar is now fixed: recording August 6, 7, 13, and 14, with August 20 held as backup; first release September 4; checkpoints September 11 and 25; final release October 2; evidence closes October 16; author and editor comments are due October 19; board decision October 22. Finance will close the pilot account October 30.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Attach the calendar to the role table and episode checklist. The evidence close allows completion and conversion measures to mature before comments are due. Finance can report committed, paid, and projected amounts separately at both checkpoints and the account close.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I signed the six-episode charter with the author, editor, production manager, and web producer. The board recorded the $9,000 ceiling and October 22 authority. The distributor settings now exclude listener profiles. We paid the studio deposit and the actor confirmed the four recording dates plus the conditional backup day.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: The production file can now be assembled from the signed charter, locked-script register, episode checklist, bank tracker, cost forecast, privacy settings, channel list, checkpoint forms, and dated board agenda. Those records give each owner the same operating reference during the season.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The board secretary has added the four format choices to the October agenda and noted that no later season or audiobook is approved by the pilot charter. The production manager will report bank and budget every Monday. The web producer has the authority to move a release that misses transcript or version checks, and I hold the pause decision after any bank or budget trigger.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: The August kickoff record now contains the first four script identifiers, studio schedule, transcript handoffs, distributor privacy setting, Monday reporting template, and the October agenda filed with the closeout definitions.
